title: Prompt weights: what the brackets really do
hook: Brackets don't multiply a word's embedding. They push it away from what the empty prompt has at that position. And some text encoders ignore them completely.

verified.claim: Each bracket pair multiplies by 1.1, and a number replaces the weight outright.
verified.ref: The lab's port equals the real token_weights on seven test strings, on a CPU

verified.claim: Weighted tokens become (z minus z_empty) times weight plus z_empty.
The pooled vector is taken from the same unweighted pass.
Several tokenizers, including Klein's and the one Qwen Image uses, pass disable_weights=True.
Backslash-escaped brackets are protected from parsing, then restored.

unchecked: No render here compares weights. All the figures come from the parser and from random stand-in rows.
We list only two tokenizers with weights off. There are others, so check your model's tokenizer rather than this list.
We don't claim how a given weight changes a picture.
